name: Emdash

surfaces.label: Emdash desktop app (Electron), stable channel: /Applications/Emdash.app/Contents/MacOS/Emdash. A HOST, not an agent: it runs the coding-agent CLIs of other vendors (claude, codex, opencode, amp and 30 more) in PTYs or over ACP, one worktree per task. The main process and up to 16 worker processes (the desktop worker manifest lists 16 ids) share this one executable (workers are fork()ed, run as node via ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, with argv[1] = .../Resources/app.asar/out/main/<name>-runtime.js), plus Electron helper processes under Contents/Frameworks. The probe keeps only the outermost match, so workers fold into the app. The hosted agents match their own registry rows, not this one.

Emdash Canary: app name 'Emdash Canary' has a space, so agents_probe.py (ps args split on spaces) sees argv[0] as just /Applications/Emdash and argv[1] as Canary.app/Contents/MacOS/Emdash. This entry keys on that split, as the zed row does for Preview. Electron helpers do not match (their argv[1] is .../Frameworks/Emdash). A detector that reads the full executable path can rely on path_contains '/Emdash Canary.app/Contents/MacOS/' instead. User data is ~/Library/Application Support/emdash-canary.

tui-agents worker: the Emdash executable running app.asar/out/main/tui-agents-runtime.js. It owns every terminal-style agent session (node-pty). Each hosted agent CLI is a DIRECT child of this pid (argv is the plain agent command, no shell, when the project has no shell setup and tmux is off). This is the pid whose direct children are agents; the main app pid's direct children are only helpers and workers. Folded into the gui surface by the probe's outermost-match rule; listed so a detector that reads full command lines can find the agent parent.

acp worker: the Emdash executable running app.asar/out/main/acp-runtime.js. It owns the structured chat (ACP, JSON-RPC over stdio) sessions. Its direct children are the ACP provider processes: for Claude Code and Codex the Emdash executable again running out/main/adapters/claude-acp.mjs or codex-acp.mjs (the path most likely sits under app.asar, not app.asar.unpacked: inferred, unobserved) (ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE / CODEX_PATH pointing at the user's own CLI); for others the CLI itself (`opencode acp`, `vibe-acp`, ...). Folded into the gui surface by the probe.

working_signals.name: ~/Library/Application Support/emdash/emdash4.db-wal
working_signals.meaning: Weak, and the only file-level signal. Emdash keeps no transcript: it stores agent status, not messages. The app database (WAL mode) has one row per conversation in table `conversations` with a device-local `agent_status` cache ('idle' | 'working' | 'awaiting-input' | 'completed' | 'error') that the app writes on each transition. Exact per-conversation truth is a read-only `SELECT id, provider, type, agent_status FROM conversations WHERE agent_status = 'working' AND location = 'local'` on that file (never select title, config or any text column). The WAL moves on a status change, not while a turn streams, and also for unrelated writes, so a quiet WAL proves nothing. Stale after a crash or a force quit: the app resets 'working' and 'awaiting-input' to 'idle' only at the next launch (boot database phase, rows with location=local of type pty and of type acp; rows of remote SSH hosts are never reset and describe agents that are not in this Mac's process table, hence the location filter). The status is hook-driven for terminal sessions, so an interrupted turn can stay 'working' (Claude Code's Stop hook does not run on a user interrupt; inferred for Emdash). Not read by agents_probe. Stable channel path; canary is ~/Library/Application Support/emdash-canary, and EMDASH_USER_DATA_DIR / EMDASH_DB_FILE override it. Never observed: Emdash is not installed here.

Last resort, unmeasured guess (Electron GUI floor from registry README section 4). The tree holds Electron renderer and GPU helpers, up to 16 node workers (git, file watcher, resource-usage polling) and every hosted agent, so typing, diffs or a build in a task terminal also raise it. Do NOT use child_process, tool_children or power_assertion on the Emdash pid: Emdash itself holds no sleep assertion (no powerSaveBlocker or caffeinate anywhere in its source), and its direct children are long-lived helpers and workers, so a child rule reads every Emdash as working forever. Better: judge each hosted agent by its own row. A hosted `claude` is a direct child of the tui-agents worker and matches the claude-code row, where its own `caffeinate` child is the precise turn signal; the transcript is ~/.claude/projects/*/<conversation id>.jsonl because Emdash launches `claude --session-id <conversation id>` (or `--resume <id>`).

waiting_signals.meaning: Read-only, same file as above. Terminal sessions: set when an installed hook reports notification_type permission_prompt, idle_prompt or elicitation_dialog. ACP chat sessions: set when the session has a pending permission request (pendingPermissionCount > 0). CAUTION: for Claude Code the status is 'awaiting-input' after idle_prompt too (its idle-waiting notification, classified by message text: not matching /permission|approval/ means idle_prompt), so 'awaiting-input' does not always mean 'blocked on a permission'. The permission-versus-idle distinction lives only in the in-memory TuiAgentState.notificationType, not in the database. A finished turn reads 'completed' first (Stop hook).

Emdash raises an in-app notification feed entry, a 'needs_attention' sound and an OS notification when a session needs attention or completes. None is readable by another process; the notification path uses Electron Notification (main/host/notifications/system-notification-sink.ts) and an in-renderer sound player, not a helper process; afplay and terminal-notifier appear nowhere in source. osascript does appear, but only for opening Terminal/iTerm on SSH tasks and listing fonts, not for notifications.

hooks.config: Emdash has no user-facing lifecycle hooks of its own. Its `.emdash.json` (and Project Settings) hold shellSetup, preservePatterns and scripts.setup/run/teardown, which are project scripts, not turn events. Emdash is instead a hook CONSUMER: before a terminal session starts it installs marker-tagged entries into the hosted agent's USER-GLOBAL config, never the worktree (Claude Code: ~/.claude/settings.json or $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json, keys SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Notification, Stop; each command is `EMDASH_HOOK_CONFIG_VERSION=1; if [ -z "${EMDASH_HOOK_PORT:-}" ] ... exit 0; fi; curl -sf -X POST ... http://127.0.0.1:$EMDASH_HOOK_PORT/hook`). The entries stay in the file for good and are no-ops outside Emdash. The running session gets EMDASH_HOOK_PORT, EMDASH_HOOK_NONCE, EMDASH_HOOK_TOKEN and EMDASH_PTY_ID (= conversation id) in its environment, and TERM_PROGRAM=emdash. Hooks or plugins are installed for 24 of 37 providers (Amp, Antigravity, Auggie, Claude Code, CodeBuddy, Codex, Command Code, Devin, Droid, GitHub Copilot, Goose, Grok, Kilocode, Kimi, Kiro, MiMo Code, Mistral Vibe, Muse Code, Oh My Pi, OpenCode, Pi, Prime Agent, Qoder CLI, Qwen Code; counted from packages/plugins/src/agents/impl/*/index.ts and the root table in agents/integrations/providers.md). Emdash does not infer status from terminal output; a provider without hooks shows no status for that event, except that an Enter keypress marks it 'working'.

telemetry.how: No OpenTelemetry. Product analytics go to PostHog (allowlisted events such as app_started, agent_run_started, agent_run_finished, plus perf_vitals), on by default in production builds, off with TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false (or 0, no) or in Settings > General > Privacy & Telemetry. Nothing to point a collector at. Git grep -i for opentelemetry, OTEL_ and otlp over all 5,194 tracked files at commit 873a3e2 matches only pnpm-lock.yaml (an optional peer dependency @opentelemetry/api of some package); no source file, package.json or config uses it.

sources.claim: Terminal-style agents are spawned by the tui-agents worker with node-pty; on macOS with no shell setup and no tmux the agent is exec'd directly, so it is a direct child of the worker. sources.claim: Status vocabulary and mapping: TUI hook events start -> working, stop -> completed, error -> error, notification with permission_prompt / idle_prompt / elicitation_dialog -> awaiting-input, other notification -> idle; ACP: pending permission -> permission notification, isGenerating -> start, stopReason -> stop or error, cancelled -> reset to idle

notes: Emdash is an orchestrator: no model loop of its own, so 'is Emdash working' means 'is at least one hosted agent working'. On the Mac the process table shows one app tree: main process, Electron helpers, up to 16 workers (same executable, argv[1] = .../app.asar/out/main/<name>-runtime.js). Only two workers matter: tui-agents-runtime.js (its direct children are the terminal agents) and acp-runtime.js (its direct children are the ACP providers). Hosted agents such as claude or codex match their own rows too; classify their state with those rows and drop any match whose ancestor is a registered Emdash pid (registry README section 3, case 12), or the same turn is counted twice. Nothing in argv marks an agent as Emdash's; use the ancestor chain, or read TERM_PROGRAM=emdash / EMDASH_PTY_ID from the process environment. The exact state is in emdash4.db (read-only `conversations.agent_status`), keyed by conversation id, which for Claude Code equals the session id. Not verified live: Emdash is not installed here, so the executable name, worker argv, idle CPU and how quickly the database reflects a turn are all read from source, not observed.
